claims.text: Plasma nitriding Zircaloy at approximately 500°C for about 1 hour will form a thin, uniform ZrN surface layer.
The in-situ-formed ZrN interlayer will function as a robust diffusion barrier between Zircaloy and the elemental Cr coating.
The ZrN interlayer will lower the mobility of zirconium into the overlying Cr coating.
Reduced Cr–Zr interdiffusion will preserve Cr-coating integrity.
Reduced Cr–Zr interdiffusion will preserve coating adhesion during high-temperature and long-term aqueous exposure.
Preserving the outer Cr layer will maintain effective oxidation protection.
Pre-nitrided, Cr-coated Zircaloy will exhibit significantly less interfacial Cr–Zr interdiffusion than conventional Cr-coated Zircaloy.
Pre-nitrided, Cr-coated Zircaloy will have better coating adhesion than conventional Cr-coated Zircaloy.
Pre-nitrided, Cr-coated Zircaloy will undergo less oxidation degradation than conventional Cr-coated Zircaloy.
The proposed ZrN interlayer will improve Cr-coating durability during transient steam exposure up to approximately 1200°C for seconds to minutes.
The proposed ZrN interlayer will improve Cr-coating durability during extended subcritical-water exposure at approximately 400°C.
The proposed coating architecture will remain beneficial under cyclic thermal-shock conditions.
Conventional elemental Cr-coated Zircaloy experiences accelerated degradation because elevated-temperature Cr–Zr interdiffusion causes coating failure.
